name: Long-Term Resident visa (定住者)

requirement_groups.name: Nikkei 2nd generation (child of a former Japanese national)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being the child of a person who was born a Japanese national and later lost that nationality (e.g. through naturalisation abroad) — 2nd-generation Nikkei descendants.

This requires being the grandchild (3rd generation) of a person born a Japanese national who later lost that nationality — the standard Teijusha route reaches 3rd-generation Nikkei descendants directly, with no sponsor or age-limited program required.

evidence_required.document: Documented descent chain (koseki or equivalent civil records linking the applicant to the qualifying Japanese-national ancestor)

outcome.duration_length: 6 months, 1 year, 3 years, or 5 years, renewable

sources.title: Immigration Services Agency of Japan — 定住者 (Long-Term Resident) status, 日系人 (Nikkei) provisions under Ministry of Justice notification (告示)

notes: GENUINE GENERATIONAL LIMIT CONFIRMED, matching the pattern of similar restrictions found elsewhere in this dataset (Portugal's 2025 parent/grandparent cap on jure sanguinis): standard, unrestricted Teijusha (Long-Term Resident) status for Nikkei descendants reaches the 3RD generation (grandchildren of a person born Japanese) with full, unrestricted work rights and no sponsor required — the SAME generational depth as Portugal's post-2025 reform, though Japan's limit has been stable long-term rather than a recent tightening. A SEPARATE, genuinely distinct 4th-generation program exists (created 2018, 特定活動 告示43号 status, not Teijusha) but is materially different: capped at ages 18-30, maximum 5 years total, REQUIRES a named Japanese sponsor ('Nikkei Yonsei Uketsuke Supporter'), and is explicitly framed as a cultural/language-learning bridge program rather than open settlement — modeled here as a scope exclusion rather than a third requirement_group, since its terminal, non-settlement nature (no leads_to_pr, no unrestricted work) makes it functionally closer to a working-holiday-style route than to the Nikkei ancestry route proper; a future pass could encode it as its own separate file (jp_nikkei_yonsei) given how structurally distinct it is. Also note: Teijusha status covers OTHER special circumstances beyond Nikkei descent (certain refugee-adjacent cases, some divorced/widowed spouses of Japanese nationals meeting residence thresholds) not modeled as separate groups here — a scope simplification, since Nikkei descent is the route's most requested and most distinctive use case for this dataset's purposes.
